A virtual office can serve as a correspondence and administrative address, but under Article 9 of Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 the statutory registered office must be located in Spain where the effective centre of management or central administration has its actual physical presence. For an ISIC 7420 stock photography and generative visual assets platform operating via Stripe and PayPal, a wholly virtual office is not sufficient to meet the statutory seat test; reliance on a virtual office materially increases the risk of an adverse Spanish tax-residence determination and a commercial substance challenge.

Stage 03
Tax Identity & Indirect Tax

      
Tax authority e-portal, entity tax classification elections, VAT thresholds, and 0% export documentation chain.

    

    

      
Tax ID Application Infrastructure

      

        
Competent tax authority
Agencia Estatal de Administracion Tributaria (AEAT) - State Tax Administration Agency; electronic portal: Sede Electronica at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; customs and excise administered by the AEAT Department of Customs and Excise (Departamento de Aduanas e Impuestos Especiales); annual tax returns filed via Modelo 200 (Corporate Income Tax), Modelo 303 (VAT), Modelo 036/037 (census registration), and Modelo 349 (recapitulative intra-EU statement).

        
E-government filing portal
The foreign-owned Spanish SL obtains its statutory Tax ID (NIF) and VAT ID as a single integrated process: (i) execute the notarial deed of incorporation, register the company in the Registro Mercantil, and obtain provisional NIF clearance from AEAT; (ii) file Modelo 036 declaracion censal to request the definitive NIF (8 digits plus control letter), choosing CNAE 7420 photographic activities and declaring the date of commencement - definitive NIF issues within one month, and the same number is the VAT registration number with the prefix 'ES' (e.g., ESB12345674); (iii) non-resident corporate shareholders without a permanent establishment additionally obtain a non-resident NIF (prefix 'N' for foreign corporations) by filing Form 030 with proof of foreign incorporation (apostilled and translated) and appointing a fiscal representative where required for non-EU entities; (iv) foreign entities selling B2C digital services into Spain may bypass local establishment and obtain a Spanish VAT ID through the non-union One-Stop-Shop route. All registration procedures require prior electronic identification by qualified certificate, DNIe, or Cl@ve PIN for submissions through the AEAT portal.

      

      
Tax ID type & application path: Entity_Level_Taxation — The foreign-owned Spanish SL obtains its statutory Tax ID (NIF) and VAT ID as a single integrated process: (i) execute the notarial deed of incorporation, register the company in the Registro Mercantil, and obtain provisional NIF clearance from AEAT; (ii) file Modelo 036 declaracion censal to request the definitive NIF (8 digits plus control letter), choosing CNAE 7420 photographic activities and declaring the date of commencement - definitive NIF issues within one month, and the same number is the VAT registration number with the prefix 'ES' (e.g., ESB12345674); (iii) non-resident corporate shareholders without a permanent establishment additionally obtain a non-resident NIF (prefix 'N' for foreign corporations) by filing Form 030 with proof of foreign incorporation (apostilled and translated) and appointing a fiscal representative where required for non-EU entities; (iv) foreign entities selling B2C digital services into Spain may bypass local establishment and obtain a Spanish VAT ID through the non-union One-Stop-Shop route. All registration procedures require prior electronic identification by qualified certificate, DNIe, or Cl@ve PIN for submissions through the AEAT portal.

    

    

      
Default Tax Classification & Elections

      

        
Default tax classification
Entity_Level_Taxation

        
Available election forms
Spain follows an opaque entity-level regime; no US-style check-the-box election exists and a Spanish SL is always a taxable person for Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Ley 27/2014) taxed at the standard 25% (15% reduced rate for newly created SLs in the first two profitable tax years subject to turnover and capital conditions, declared via Modelo 036). Available statutory elections include: (i) consolidated tax group regime (arts. 58-70 LIS) for groups with direct or indirect 75% voting control, irrevocable for three years; (ii) patent box election (art. 23 LIS) granting 50% exemption on qualifying IP exploitation income; (iii) ETVE holding-company election giving a territorial exemption for foreign-source dividends and capital gains; (iv) EU ATAD hybrid-mismatch adjustments (art. 15 quaterdecies LIS) which are mandatory rather than elective; (v) for indirect tax, the Union OSS and non-Union OSS elections covering cross-border B2C supply of electronic and stock-photo services. Any election affecting the tax base is filed with the definitive NIF application and updated via Modelo 036 whenever circumstances change.

      

    

    

      
VAT / GST & 0% Export Zero-Rating

      

        
Standard VAT / GST rate
21%

        
Mandatory registration threshold (Nexus)
No general registration threshold exists in Spain: any person performing taxable supplies, including digital stock-photo licensing and generative visual-asset sales, must register for VAT from the first euro of turnover. A registration threshold of EUR 10,000 per calendar year applies only to intra-Community distance and B2C electronic-service sales into other EU Member States (Union OSS threshold); below EUR 10,000 the supply is subject to Spanish 21% VAT. Non-EU service providers selling digital services to Spanish consumers must register for Spanish VAT via the non-union OSS with no local turnover threshold.

      

      
      

        Export 0% zero-rating conditions
        
Exports of physical goods to third countries and territories (including Ceuta and Melilla) qualify for the 0% rate (exemption with credit, art. 21.1 LIVA) when the goods physically leave EU customs territory within 90 days of dispatch and the exporter holds a validated customs export declaration (DUA). The 0% rate also covers ancillary transport, loading, insurance, and other services directly related to exported goods (art. 21.2 LIVA). For B2B stock-photo licensing, AI-generated visual assets, and digital marketplace services supplied to non-EU business customers, the place of supply is the customer's country (art. 69.1 LIVA); Spanish VAT is not chargeable and the transaction, if still reportable, is captured in Modelo 349 recapitulative returns. B2C digital services to non-EU consumers are placed where the consumer is established or resides (outside the EU) and therefore fall outside Spanish VAT. Zero-rating eligibility requires documentary proof of export or foreign-recipient status rather than mere assertion of non-domicile, and AEAT applies a business-reality test examining substance, pricing, and payment flows.

        
    
          
          
  • Customs Export Declaration (DUA) with CUSDEC/AAR confirmation and customs officer's exit validation (prueba de exportacion), including 14-digit MRN where applicable
    • 
          
          
  • Bill of Lading or Air Waybill for sea/air freight, or CMR waybill for road transport, evidencing physical departure from EU territory, with signed proof of delivery (POD) for DDP and DAP terms
    • 
          
          
  • Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103/credit confirmation from the Spanish or EU-acquired banking channel evidencing actual collection of export proceeds
    • 
          
          
  • Commercial invoice compliant with RD 1619/2012, containing complete service/goods description, quantity, unit price, INCOTERMS, exemption legenda (Exportacion exenta art. 21 LIVA), and recipient VAT/GST ID
    • 
          
          
  • Contractual scope-of-rights documentation for stock-photo and AI-visual licensing (royalty schedules, usage restrictions, territorial grant, and download/revenue evidence from the platform), together with Modelo 349 recapitulative records and, where applicable, the certificate of transferability of the transaction to the platform operator
    • 
          
        

      

      
      
Real-time fiscal clearance is mandatory through the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Informacion) for large taxpayers (turnover above EUR 6 million), VAT groups, and entities in certain regimes: invoice records G1-G4 must be transmitted electronically to AEAT within 4 calendar days of issue (8 calendar days for third-party issued invoices), using the XSD/TEDE schemas and qualified electronic certificates. The Veri*factu regime (Ley 18/2022 Crea y Crece, RD 1007/2023) obliges all billing software to generate a hash-chain integrity record with timestamps and a QR verification code (codigo VERI); software providers must be compliant by 1 July 2025 and all end-user businesses by 1 January 2026. B2B electronic invoicing in Facturae format is mandated for issuers with turnover above EUR 8 million from 1 July 2025 and for all businesses from 1 January 2026, unless the issuer already reports bills through SII or Veri*factu. Non-compliance blocks VAT refunds and exposes the company to AEAT electronic-settlement penalty rules.

      
AEAT audit teams actively target fictitious and inflated export zero-rating schemes, using risk flags such as related-party buyers, cycles through letterbox intermediaries, sales to high-risk territories, pricing outside arm's length range, and funds cleared through PayPal/Stripe without correspondent Spanish banking entry. Consequences of a challenge include: (i) immediate VAT assessment at 21% with statutory late-payment interest, plus the art. 27 LGT surcharge of 1%-20% for late payment; (ii) penalty under art. 191 LGT of 50%-150% of the tax loss, aggravated for intentional conduct; (iii) independent penalty of 50% of the invoice amount (minimum EUR 150) under art. 201 LGT for invoices containing false or misleading data; (iv) fines of EUR 300 to EUR 6,000 per record for omission or incorrect SII/Veri*factu transmission (art. 193 LGT); (v) retrospective clawback of VAT refunds and credit offsets for up to 4 years under the statute of limitations (arts. 66-70 LGT), with unlimited reassessment where the declarant operates through a tax-haven jurisdiction; (vi) criminal referral under art. 305 CP for evasion exceeding EUR 120,000 (imprisonment 2-6 years and fine up to six times the defrauded amount), and under art. 305 bis CP for organized VAT-fraud circuits exceeding EUR 2,000,000 (imprisonment 5-9 years); (vii) removal from the OSS special scheme, revocation of clean-tax certificates, prohibition on public subsidies and concession contracts, and director disqualification for the SL's administrators. Companies using Spanish export zero-rating must therefore retain the full evidentiary bundle for at least the 4-year limitation period and align payment receipt and FX repatriation with the 180-day benchmark to rebut the presumption of fictitious export.

Stage 04
Banking & Treasury Architecture

      
Central-bank FX diagnosis, tier-1 local banks vs offshore digital EMI matrix, and KYC rejection defense guide.

    

    

      
Foreign Exchange Regime & Central Bank Policy

      

        
Current-account convertibility
Spain is a eurozone member state with full liberalization of capital movements under Articles 63-66 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the Spanish Royal Decree-Law 1116/1991 on capital transactions. Current account and capital account convertibility are unrestricted for euro and foreign currency transactions, subject to compliance reporting to the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments Registry for transactions exceeding EUR 50,000 or as statutorily required. Dividend and profit remittances by a Spanish SL to non-resident shareholders are freely permitted after corporate tax and withholding tax obligations are satisfied, provided proof of tax residence, beneficial ownership declarations, and anti-money laundering source-of-funds documentation is submitted to the remitting bank. Hurdles are primarily documentary, not exchange control, and include the obligation to file the annual 'Declaración de Operaciones con el Exterior' (form C-1) for certain cross-border flows, and the need to present valid tax clearance certificates where required by banking compliance.

        
Export proceeds surrender rules
No statutory export proceeds surrender requirement exists in Spain for euro-denominated receipts or foreign currency receipts. As a eurozone member, Spain has no mandatory conversion ratio or compulsory repatriation timeline for export proceeds. Exporters are, however, required to maintain due documentary support for customs, VAT, and balance of payments declaration purposes and must file the corresponding cross-border transaction declarations with the Bank of Spain when thresholds apply. For stock photo licensing and AI-generated visual asset sales, proceeds received via acquiring platforms (e.g., Stripe, PayPal) are treated as ordinary trade receipts and are freely retained or converted at any licensed bank, subject to standard AML/KYC verification and accurate reflection in the entity's statutory accounting records.

      

      
Central bank supervision: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), operating within the European System of Central Banks and under the prudential supervision framework of the Single Supervisory Mechanism for euro area credit institutions

    

    

      
Offshore Digital Bank / EMI Whitelist

      

        
        

          

            Cross-border EMI / Fintech rails
            Fit: High
          

          
Feasibility rating for offshore fintech and Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) is Medium with significant legal constraints. A Spanish SL may open accounts with EU-licensed EMIs operating in Spain under the freedom to provide services or through a Spanish branch; however, such accounts are not a full substitute for a bank account at a credit institution in Spain for purposes of capital increase escrow, trade finance, or certain high-volume payouts. EMIs cannot accept deposits and are not covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund, which elevates counterparty and treasury risk. Offshore non-EU EMIs are generally impractical for primary treasury operations due to Spanish regulatory expectations of a domestic or EU-passported entity, AML equivalence, and the risk of being characterized as unauthorized deposit-taking if structured improperly. Best practice is to use an EMI solely as an auxiliary receivables collection rail while maintaining a primary clearing account with a Tier-1 Spanish commercial bank.

Core KYC Rejection Triggers & Defense Dossier

      
      

        Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner with complex shareholding structure
        
Root cause: Non-resident ultimate beneficial owner with complex shareholding structure

        
Defense evidence: Full ownership chain chart, certified corporate registers from each jurisdiction, valid passports of all natural-person UBOs, proof of ultimate source of wealth, audited financial statements or independent wealth evidence, and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for the tiered holding structure.

      

      
      

        High-frequency cross-border receivables from distributed online marketplaces (Stripe, PayPal, stock content aggregators)
        
Root cause: High-frequency cross-border receivables from distributed online marketplaces (Stripe, PayPal, stock content aggregators)

        
Defense evidence: Executed platform service agreements, historical transaction ledgers evidencing genuine commercial activity, VAT registration certificate, ISIC 7420 activity description, customer geolocation breakdown, payout reconciliation reports, and a compliance narrative aligning payment flow origin with the digital content licensing business model.

      

      
      

        Distributed royalty or licensing payouts to foreign content creators and AI generation subcontractors
        
Root cause: Distributed royalty or licensing payouts to foreign content creators and AI generation subcontractors

        
Defense evidence: Written licensing agreements, model releases, AI training provenance documentation, subcontractor KYC files, evidence of withholding tax or reverse-charge VAT handling, and a documented business rationale for each cross-border beneficiary to refute money laundering or undisclosed related-party structuring.

      

      
      

        IP-intensive asset base with no physical inventory and low tangible asset footprint
        
Root cause: IP-intensive asset base with no physical inventory and low tangible asset footprint

        
Defense evidence: Copyright registrations, digital asset custody records, developer and creator contracts, bank statements demonstrating revenue generation, tax return filings, and board minutes confirming the operational substance of the stock photo AI platform in Spain.

      

      
    

    

      
Cross-Border Clearing Corridors & Settlement Fit

      

        Compliant inbound capital injections to a Spanish SL must be executed via the Spanish entity's IBAN account at a licensed credit institution, using SWIFT wire with a detailed beneficiary reference. For share capital equity injections, the sender must indicate a payment purpose consistent with the Companies Law and the notarial capital increase if applicable; common references include 'Aportación de capital social', 'Capital increase resolution', or 'Transferencia de fondos propios'. The receiving bank will require the capital increase public deed, the certificate from the Commercial Registry if amounts exceed the ordinary capitalization threshold, and the NIF of the receiving entity. Cross-border funding exceeding EUR 50,000 must be reported to the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments statistical registry, either through the bank's automatic reporting (C-1 form) or via the obligatory declaration. Failing to properly document the purpose code or submit the compliant deed may trigger AML intervention or temporary freezing.Outbound trade disbursements for stock photo and generative asset purchases from foreign suppliers, photographer royalties, AI infrastructure vendors, and platform fees should be settled primarily through SWIFT MT103 single customer credit transfers for non-urgent payments, with correspondent banking fees pre-agreed. Larger or invoice-backed disbursements may be routed via commercial letters of credit (documentary credits) under UCP 600 where the counterparty requires secure delivery against payment; however, for low-risk digital content licensing, MT103 and SEPA instant credit transfers are the standard cost-efficient rails. EUR-denominated payments to EU counterparties should use the SEPA Credit Transfer scheme with mandatory IBAN and BIC validation. Cross-border payments in non-euro currencies require accurate SWIFT message formatting, ISO 20022 compliance, and inclusion of the relevant trade invoice reference to satisfy Spanish foreign transaction reporting.Outright press or plain vanilla currency forward contracts against EUR for major convertible currencies (USD, GBP, JPY) executed with a Spanish licensed bank or EU-passported investment firmNon-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging market currencies where the underlying receivables arise from non-convertible jurisdictions or where settlement cannot be physically executed due to regulatory constraintsCross-currency interest rate swaps solely for balance sheet hedging of any mapped external debt denominated in a non-euro currency, subject to EMIR clearing and reporting thresholdsFX options (European style) for protecting downside on forecasted USD or GBP income streams while retaining upside participation
      

      
E-commerce / gateway settlement fit: Feasibility rating for offshore fintech and Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) is Medium with significant legal constraints. A Spanish SL may open accounts with EU-licensed EMIs operating in Spain under the freedom to provide services or through a Spanish branch; however, such accounts are not a full substitute for a bank account at a credit institution in Spain for purposes of capital increase escrow, trade finance, or certain high-volume payouts. EMIs cannot accept deposits and are not covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund, which elevates counterparty and treasury risk. Offshore non-EU EMIs are generally impractical for primary treasury operations due to Spanish regulatory expectations of a domestic or EU-passported entity, AML equivalence, and the risk of being characterized as unauthorized deposit-taking if structured improperly. Best practice is to use an EMI solely as an auxiliary receivables collection rail while maintaining a primary clearing account with a Tier-1 Spanish commercial bank.

Statutory Filing Calendar

              Depósito de Cuentas Anuales (Annual Accounts Filing)
              Approval by the shareholders' meeting within 6 months of fiscal year-end (30 June for 31 December year-end); deposit within one month after approval, no later than 31 July.
              $140 USD
              Registry file closure, denial of future registrations and good-standing certificates until the filing is made; repeated non-deposit may trigger administrative action and potential deregistration after 6 consecutive years.
            

            
            

              Impuesto sobre Sociedades (Corporate Income Tax Return, Modelo 200)
              Within 25 calendar days following the six-month post close of the fiscal year; for calendar-year entities, from 1 to 25 July of the following year.
              $0 USD
              Late filing surcharge of 5% up to 20% of the tax due, plus monthly late-payment interest; omission after official request triggers a fixed fine from €200 and further penalties up to 20% of undeclared amounts.
            

            
            

              Declaración de Titulares Reales (UBO Annual Confirmation)
              Concurrent with annual accounts filing, generally by 31 July following the fiscal year end; must also be updated within one month of any UBO change.
              $0 USD
              Infringements of Law 10/2010 attract fines from €600 to €60,000; non-filing also leaves the registry file in a non-compliant status, blocking corporate registrations.
            

            
            

              Modelo 347 – Declaración Anual de Operaciones con Terceras Personas (Annual Third-Party Transaction Report)
              Between 1 and 20 February for the preceding tax year; filing is required only if cumulative annual transactions with any counterparty exceed €3,000.
              $0 USD
              Fine of €200 per omitted form plus an additional penalty of up to 0.5% of the undeclared amounts; both capped under the General Tax Law.

Transfer Pricing & Economic Substance

      
Master / Local File threshold: 20,000,000 EUR (net turnover threshold triggering local file)

      
Economic substance scope: Spain's Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) require adequate local operations for certain entities and activities

      

    

    

      
Fatal Compliance Red Lines & Director Liability

      
      

        Tax Evasion
        
Statutory sanction: Criminal penalties up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 3 times evaded tax; administrative fines up to 100% of evaded tax

        
Director personal liability: Personal criminal liability, disqualification from management roles, and joint liability for tax debts

      

      
      

        Failure to Comply with Transfer Pricing Rules
        
Statutory sanction: Administrative fines 1,000-5,000 EUR per transaction or 100% of tax advantage; criminal sanctions in aggravated cases

        
Director personal liability: Personal fines and possible imprisonment for fraudulent conduct; directors liable for TP adjustments

      

      
      

        Improper Profit Repatriation / Dividend Withholding
        
Statutory sanction: Fines up to 100% of unpaid WHT plus interest; criminal prosecution for willful non-compliance

        
Director personal liability: Directors personally liable for the tax and penalties; potential jail time for evasion

      

      
      

        Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
        
Statutory sanction: Company dissolution, fines up to 1,000,000 EUR, and potential criminal sanctions under tax and AML laws

        
Director personal liability: Personal liability for damages, fines, and criminal charges for fraudulent incorporation or management
